answer: Each identity registers one crystal jar sealed with an ivory stopper, posts a 70-credit bond and files its nectar mass. An auditor reweighs the jar, subtracts the crystal tare, and accepts it only when the recomputed nectar mass matches within 2%. The first jar costs 31; the kth costs 31+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6025 and 1000 fake identities pay 3,028,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked bonds, with no bulk discount. A rented-jar ring fails because one ivory stopper serial cannot seal two jars: a reused serial burns both bonds, while an honest keeper pays 31 once and keeps the bond.
